name: MongoDB

inputs.name: uri
inputs.label: MongoDB URI without credentials (mongodb+srv://host/?... or mongodb://host:27017/?...)

access: role read on the database (find on the collection), for a user of the admin database
error_hint: MongoDB's adapter reports a wrong password, an address the server does not accept (Atlas: this computer's public IP must be in the project's IP access list) and an unreachable server all as 'error while reading collection metadata', and a database the account may not read as a collection that 'does not exist' - check the user and password, the access list and the database's role
tips: The collection is the upper-case root table (MOVIES); its fields and the child tables keep MongoDB's spelling, so quote them: "MOVIES_writers_arr"."_value".
A child table joins its root on "_parent" = root."_id"; mongo_id is the document's ObjectId.
Columns come from a sample of the documents: after the collection's shape changes, run exakit source refresh <name>.
notes: One virtual schema per collection: its root table, plus a child table for each nested object and array (measured on sample_mflix.movies: 12 tables). The schema is inferred from a bounded sample.

The URI carries no credentials: the user and password go into the CONNECTION, where the database keeps them hidden; a URI with user:password@ is refused. Atlas mongodb+srv:// addresses resolve from inside the database (measured).
Needs the Rust language container (exasol-labs/language-container-rs 0.33.0, pinned per CPU architecture): exakit connect installs it with your consent and restarts the database once.
The adapter needs only MongoDB's find permission on the collection (read on the database).

The adapter always signs in against the admin database: it gives the CONNECTION's user and password as the credential, which replaces any authSource in the URI, so a URI or connection string with another authSource is refused. Keep authSource=admin (or leave it out) so the URI says the same, and make the reader a user of admin (an Atlas database user always is).
Atlas answers only addresses in the project's IP access list: add this computer's public IP as a permanent entry. A temporary entry stops the source when it expires.
